steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
Schedules scattered across notes, chats and notices are easy to miss. Today you'll gather them into one schedule table and add them to your calendar in one go.

Scattered notesClaudeSchedule tablesettle clashesCalendar file (.ics)importYour calendar
For Claude Code to edit your calendar directly, you'd need extra connection setup. Today you'll skip that and make an .ics file that calendars can read.
  • Time: 20 minutes
  • You need: a computer where you've done Work 1, and a Google, Outlook or Apple calendar

steps.title: Get the sample schedule notes
steps.html:
Notes written on Monday, November 23. Dates are written every which way, and there's 'next Tuesday'-style wording that needs a reference date, plus a hidden clash.

⬇ Download the sample schedule.txt

Drag schedule.txt from Downloads into the Practice folder.

check.q: Is schedule.txt in the Practice folder?

steps.title: If getting the file doesn't work
steps.html:
• If clicking shows text on screen, save it with Ctrl+S (⌘+S on a Mac) as schedule.txt.
  • Moving works like in Work 1.

steps.title: Start with a new chat
steps.html: Claude app → Code tab → + New. Check the buttons under the typing box show Local · Practice · Manual.

check.q: Can you see Local · Practice · Manual?

steps.title: If the start screen looks different
steps.html:
• If the folder isn't Practice, click the folder button → Open folder… and choose it.
  • Click the permission mode button and choose Manual.

steps.title: Gather everything into a dated table
steps.html: To turn 'next Tuesday' into a real date, it needs to know what day it is today. Use the day the notes were written (November 23). And ask it to flag clashes and unclear items separately.
steps.alt: Events gathered into a dated table, flagging a clash and an unclear date
steps.code: Today is Monday, November 23, 2026. Put schedule.txt into a table by date, and flag anything that clashes or is unclear

check.q: Did it flag the 12/1 10 a.m. clash and that 'Monday of the 2nd week' is unclear?

steps.title: If it missed the clash
steps.html:
• From Monday, November 23, 'next Tuesday' is December 1. It clashes with the bank visit (December 1, 10 a.m.).
  • 'Monday of the 2nd week of December' is December 7 by calendar rows, or December 14 as the second Monday, so a person has to decide.
  • Try: "Recalculate the date for 'next Tuesday' and check for events at the same time on the same day."

steps.title: You decide the clashes; then save
steps.html: The AI can spot them, but you make the call. Tell it your decisions and save the schedule to a file. Read the create-file card and click Allow.
steps.code: Make the workshop December 7. I'll move the bank visit to 2 p.m. on December 1. Save the updated schedule as schedule.csv

check.q: Is there a schedule.csv in the Practice folder?

steps.title: If you don't see the file
steps.html:
• If you denied the card, send it again and allow it.
  • Close the folder window and open it again.

steps.title: See just next week
steps.html: With a schedule table, you can pull out just "this week" or "next week".
steps.code: From schedule.csv, show only next week's events (11/30–12/6), by day

check.q: Did you get 12/1 marketing meeting (10 a.m.) and bank (2 p.m.), 12/3 briefing and 12/4 party?

steps.title: If events are missing or wrong
steps.html: Start with "Read schedule.csv again and…". If the bank is still at 10 a.m., the earlier change wasn't saved: "Change the bank visit to 2 p.m. on December 1 and save again."

steps.title: Make a calendar file (.ics)
steps.html: An .ics file is an event file that Google, Outlook and Apple calendars can all read. Be clear about the time zone and all-day events. Read the create-file card and click Allow.
steps.code: Turn schedule.csv into a calendar file, schedule.ics. Use my local time zone, make items without a time all-day events, and make the year-end event span 12/10–12/31

check.q: Is there a schedule.ics in the Practice folder?

steps.title: If the file wasn't created
steps.html:
• If you denied the card, send it again and allow it.
  • If Claude only showed it in the chat: "Save that as schedule.ics."

steps.title: Import it — into a 'Practice' calendar first
steps.html:
Mixed into your real calendar, practice events are a pain to remove. Create a new 'Practice' calendar and import there. Deleting that calendar later removes the practice events too.

Google CalendarIn a computer browser → ⚙ Settings at the top right → Add calendar → Create new calendar (name: Practice) → Import & export on the left → choose schedule.ics → calendar Practice → Import
OutlookDouble-click schedule.ics, or File → Open & Export → Import/Export
Mac · iPhoneOn a Mac, double-click schedule.ics and choose a calendar. On iPhone, email the file to yourself and open it

Menu names vary a little by version.
steps.alt: Importing schedule.ics into a Practice calendar from the calendar's import screen

check.q: Did the events show up in the Practice calendar?

steps.title: If the import doesn't work
steps.html:
• Times look off? It's the time zone: "Remake schedule.ics with my time zone stated explicitly."
  • Can't read the file? "Check schedule.ics follows the standard iCalendar format and fix it."
  • If things went in wrong, delete the Practice calendar to clean up in one go.

steps.title: 🎉 Work practice 6 done! What you learned
steps.html:
Scattered notes became a schedule table and went into your calendar in one go.

Three things to remember

  1. With words like 'next week' or 'this Friday', give today's date.
  2. The AI spots clashes and unclear items; you decide.
  3. Use an .ics file to add to calendars, and test in a Practice calendar first.

Try it like this

Whenever you get a notice or minutes: "Add the events here to schedule.csv" → at the weekend: "Next week's events as .ics". Need reminders? "Add a 30-minute reminder to every event."
